children.text: atadābhatayā tasyā nākṣavadviṣayaḥ sa tu(aṇavaḥ) // Āp_1 //
children.translated_text: since it does not appear as such in that [cognition], that [atom] is not an object [of cognition], like the sense organ. // Āp_1 //

body.translated_text: Even if the graspable aspect (i.e., atoms) were the cause of sense-cognition (<s>indriya-vijñapti</s>),

children.text: yadābhāsā na tasmāt sā dravyābhāvāt dvicandravat /
children.translated_text: Since [cognition] does not appear as that [aggregate], and because there is no [corresponding] real substance, like the two moons;

children.text: evaṃ bāhyadvayañcaiva na yuktaṃ matigocaraḥ // Āp_2 //
children.translated_text: thus neither of the two external [entities] is a fitting object of cognition. // Āp_2 //
Some indeed maintain that the aggregate form is the means of proof;
but the atomic form is not the object of cognition, like hardness and the like. // Āp_3 //
If that were so, cognition of a pot, a saucer, and the like would be the same;
if [you say] the difference is due to difference of form—there is no real substance in the atom. // Āp_4 //

children.text: pramāṇabhedābhāvāt saḥ, adravye 'sti tataḥ sa hi /
children.translated_text: That [difference exists] because there is no distinction of valid cognition [for atoms]; therefore it exists in the non-substantial;
for when atoms are excluded, the cognition appearing as that [aggregate] becomes disrupted. // Āp_5 //
But that which is an internal knowable form that appears as if external—
that is the object [of cognition], because it has the nature of cognition and also because it serves as the condition for that [cognition]. // Āp_6 //
One aspect is the condition, due to its being inseparable, or due to the bestowal of capacity successively;
for that which has the form of capacity due to the influence of cooperative conditions—that is the sense organ. // Āp_7 //
And that [capacity] is not contradicted by cognition; thus the object-form
operates from beginningless time, and the capacity [acts] in mutual causation. // Āp_8 //

body.translated_text: Thus the verses of the treatise <s>Ālambanaparīkṣā</s> composed by <s>Ācārya Dignāga</s> are completed.
